case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Synthetic responses distinguished from human empirical evidence, with an authorised research/ethics scope for the changed design.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: Under Protocol v1.1, an enforceable prohibition protects the critical risk: N021 s.2.4.2 prohibits conducting research outside ethics approval and prohibits fabrication, falsification, or misrepresentation, while N001 requires AI transparency and disclosure of limitations.
case_summary.case_note: Curtin prohibits conducting research outside approved ethics scope and prohibits fabrication, falsification, or misrepresentation (N021 s.2.4.2, N145 s.3.1.3), while N001 mandates AI transparency, human oversight, and disclosure of limitations. Substituting AI-simulated responses for approved human participants without ethics authorisation or disclosure is therefore enforceably prohibited (D5=3, Critical gap=No). Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15.

documents_checked.document_title: Curtin University AI Use in Research
documents_checked.text:
AI tools can enhance research by quickly summarising or refining text, analysing large data sets, crafting and debugging code, communicating research
results and streamlining repetitive tasks. To use them well, researchers need to protect intellectual integrity and authorship, safeguard intellectual
property (including Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property), use data in culturally appropriate ways, and keep human oversight and expert
judgement at the centre of their work. AI tools must never substitute for human critical thinking, expertise and evaluation.
The guidelines apply to all Curtin researchers, including research students in master and doctoral programs. They cover generative AI tools for text,
images, audio, code and data, as well as generative AI-driven support platforms. They should be read alongside Curtin’s Artificial Intelligence Policy and
the policies of publishers, funders and governments relevant to your research.
